name: Java Virtual Threads & Structured Concurrency
tagline: Lightweight JVM-scheduled threads (Project Loom) multiplexed onto a ForkJoinPool of OS carrier threads, scaling imperative I/O to 100k+ tasks.
purpose: Build a progressive mental model of Java 21+ Virtual Threads—from carrier-thread unmounting and Java 21-23 synchronized pinning hazards to Semaphores for DB pools and StructuredTaskScope.

spark.summary: Java 21+ Virtual Threads (Project Loom) are lightweight, JVM-scheduled threads multiplexed onto a small ForkJoinPool of OS carrier threads. Blocking I/O unmounts the virtual thread instead of blocking an OS thread—unless pinned by synchronized blocks (fixed in Java 24+) or JNI.
spark.keyTakeaway: To guarantee worst-case bounds under adversarial inputs, never pool virtual threads—spawn one per task; replace `synchronized` around I/O with `ReentrantLock` on Java 21-23 to avoid carrier-thread pinning, and use StructuredTaskScope for fan-out/fan-in.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** Traditional platform threads map 1:1 to OS kernel threads (`~1 MB` stack each), capping Spring/Tomcat servers at ~200–500 concurrent requests.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Virtual Thread Mount / Unmount & Carrier Pinning State Machine (MOUNTED (Carrier) -> UNMOUNTED (Heap) -> PINNED (Hazard)); Virtual Threads Protected by Downstream Semaphore (10k Virtual Threads -> Semaphore(32) -> Carrier OS Pool -> Postgres (Max 32)).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Compare JVM Project Loom against reactive pipelines and Go's M:N runtime. When migrating a Spring Boot service to virtual threads, enable `-Djdk.tracePinnedThreads=short` (or JFR `jdk.VirtualThreadPinned` events) in staging to catch legacy JDBC drivers.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Explore concrete Spring migration guides, JDBC pool sizing, ThreadLocal leak prevention, and JVM GC.

learningJourney.title: What are Java Virtual Threads

explanation.foundation: Traditional platform threads map 1:1 to OS kernel threads (`~1 MB` stack each), capping Spring/Tomcat servers at ~200–500 concurrent requests. **Java 21+ Virtual Threads (Project Loom)** are cheap JVM-managed continuations (`~few KB`) multiplexed onto a small `ForkJoinPool` of **carrier OS threads**.
explanation.core: When a virtual thread hits blocking I/O (`Socket`, `LockSupport`), the JVM **unmounts** its stack chunk onto the heap and frees the carrier OS thread to run another virtual thread—scaling imperative blocking code to `100,000+` concurrent tasks.

ideas.title: Never Pool Virtual Threads
ideas.description: Virtual threads are cheap, disposable tasks—never wrap them in a fixed `Executors.newFixedThreadPool`. Use `Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor()` and bound *downstream resources* with a `Semaphore`.

ideas.title: Avoid `ThreadLocal` Bloat
ideas.description: Caching large buffers (e.g., 64 KB `SimpleDateFormat` or Jackson buffers) in `ThreadLocal` across 100,000 virtual threads explodes heap! Prefer immutable `ScopedValue`.

decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: To guarantee worst-case bounds under adversarial inputs, never pool virtual threads—spawn one per task; replace `synchronized` around I/O with `ReentrantLock` on Java 21-23 to avoid carrier-thread pinning, and use StructuredTaskScope for fan-out/fan-in.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.
